record.paper_title: Frequently hypercyclic operators: recent advances and open problems
record.original_question: If T is a frequently hypercyclic operator on a topological vector space X, can the set FHC(T)∪{0} itself be a linear subspace of X? Here FHC(T) is the set of frequently hypercyclic vectors of T.

evidence.quote:
Problem 6. Can the set FHC (T ) ∪ { 0} be a linear subspace of X if T is frequently
hypercyclic?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $\mathbb{K}\in\{\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}\}$ and let $T:X\to X$ be a continuous linear operator. A vector $x\in X$ is called frequently hypercyclic for $T$ if for every nonempty open set $U\subset X$ the set $\{n\in\mathbb{N}: T^n x\in U\}$ has positive lower density, i.e.
$$\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\#\{1\le n\le N: T^n x\in U\}>0.$$
Denote by $\mathrm{FHC}(T)$ the set of all frequently hypercyclic vectors of $T$, and assume that $T$ is frequently hypercyclic (so $\mathrm{FHC}(T)\neq\varnothing$).

Question: Does there exist such a pair $(X,T)$ for which the set $\mathrm{FHC}(T)\cup\{0\}$ is a linear subspace of $X$? Equivalently, can it happen that the sum of any two frequently hypercyclic vectors of $T$ is either $0$ or again frequently hypercyclic, and any nonzero scalar multiple of a frequently hypercyclic vector is again frequently hypercyclic?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether $\mathrm{FHC}(T)\cup\{0\}$ can itself be a linear subspace appears in current surveys and recent works on linear dynamics as an open problem. Related but weaker results are known: for various frequently hypercyclic operators $\mathrm{FHC}(T)\cup\{0\}$ is known to contain large linear or even closed infinite-dimensional subspaces (frequently hypercyclic subspaces), but $P(D)$ on $H(\mathbb{C})$ is frequently hypercyclic without admitting a frequently hypercyclic subspace. No source found resolves the stronger question of $\mathrm{FHC}(T)\cup\{0\}$ being an entire subspace.

status_evidence.title: Linear dynamical systems (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys open problems in linear dynamics, including structural questions about the set of frequently hypercyclic vectors.
status_evidence.claim: The structural/linearity questions about FHC(T) remain among open problems in the area.

status_evidence.title: Non-existence of frequently hypercyclic subspaces for P(D)
status_evidence.snippet: Shows that P(D) on H(C) is frequently hypercyclic but admits no frequently hypercyclic subspace.
status_evidence.claim: Related subspace problem partially answered in negative direction, but the stronger question of whether FHC(T)∪{0} can itself be a subspace is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Frequent hypercyclicity of weighted composition operators on C^∞
status_evidence.snippet: Shows FHC(C_{w,ψ})∪{0} contains a closed infinite-dimensional subspace for certain weighted composition operators.
status_evidence.claim: FHC(T)∪{0} is known to contain large subspaces in specific cases, but not known to be a subspace.
